problem: Find the real part of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}].$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Vector
examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071291/assets/e482e62cbd229d5d7d86010ab39fea9c56ba4b1dc7bd0553cbfbb6a2fbfc8398.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071291/assets/f4542dad2dfcb51cd14caff63d99064d8a8e98772a58d4ab4022d2b572a1aad9.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071291/assets/8e644a1eabc085ec8e7087e07d0e5860ebf1808a63747d4f9196e08b08dd72ce.png) what is the value of $ab+cd?$
examples.worked_solution:
For the given vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071291/assets/1751b58c55d6a2d44458a084d8beb31862afb4746645f10cfa04198a583f509e.png) we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $a=-3, b=5, c=7$ and $d=-2,$ which implies that

$$
ab+cd=(-3) \cdot 5 + 7 \cdot (-2) = -29.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}3+2\text{i} \\ 1-\text{i} \\ 5-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{3+2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{1-\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{5-3\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3-2\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 5+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
